1101: You must expand to survive. You have a small, cheap ark and an engine that travels at Warp 6 without fuel. Your population grows twice as fast as the chosen rate, but the maximum population of each planet is halved. The Metamorph hull and the Flux amplifier are reserved for you, but you cannot build stargates.
1103: You cross enemy territory unseen. All your ships have 75% built-in cloaking, and cargo does not reduce it. Stealth bomber and Marauder hulls, stealth components, and two sensors able to steal minerals from enemy fleets and planets. You cross minefields one Warp step faster without risk, and you passively spy on the others' research.
1105: You dominate the battlefield. Your colonists attack better, your ships are faster in combat and your weapons cost 25% less. You start with Weapons 6, Energy 1 and Propulsion 1, and will be able to build the Heavy cruiser and the Leviathan. On the other hand, you can only build basic planetary defenses and no minelayers.
1107: You are an expert at manipulating environments. You start with Biotechnology 6 and a ship able to terraform from orbit. Your bombs can un-terraform enemy worlds. Terraforming costs you nothing, planets you leave return to their original environment, and each planet has up to a 10% chance per year to permanently improve one environment variable by 1%.
1109: You are tough. Your colonists repel invasions better, your ships repair twice as fast, and you have unique protections and slowing minefields (harrows). Planetary defenses 40% cheaper, weapons 25% more expensive. Your colonists breed at half speed in your freighters. Your peaceful people refuse targeted bombs.
1111: You are experts in minefields. You start with two minelayers, Propulsion 2 and Biotechnology 2. Your fields decay more slowly, detect enemy ships and can be laid on the move, and your standard fields can be detonated remotely. You cross enemy fields two Warp steps faster without risk.
1113: You excel at launching mineral packets. You start with Energy 4, a Warp 5 mass driver on your station and a second planet. Your packets are smaller and cheaper, decay more slowly, carry a penetrating scanner, and can terraform the target if they are not fully caught.
1115: You excel at stargates. You start with Propulsion 5 and Construction 5, an assortment of ships and a second planet, both equipped with stargates. Your ships go through stargates with their cargo and take less risk when exceeding the limits. Stargates 25% cheaper; they scan enemy planets with stargates within range. Your mass drivers, on the other hand, are mediocre.
1117: Your people live in orbit in their stations (20% cheaper) and cannot live on planets. If the station is destroyed, the whole colony dies. No planetary installations, but an innate mining and detection ability, and remote mining of your own worlds. Maximum population depends on the station, production on habitability and Energy level. You will be able to build the World fortress.
1119: Your race does not specialize in any field. You start at level 3 in all technologies with a wide assortment of ships. Your Picket, Frigate and Destroyer hulls have a built-in penetrating scanner that improves with Electronics. Your maximum population per planet is 20% higher.
1121: Access to the Economizer and Galactic ramscoop engines, +1 Propulsion level at the start. All engines use 15% less fuel.
1123: Additional terraforming technologies through Biotechnology, from ±3% on all three variables up to ±30%. Terraforming costs 30% less.
1125: Three mining hulls and two additional robots. You start with two Dwarf miners.
1127: Two new stations: the Orbital dock, cheap with a small shipyard, and the Orbital citadel. Your stations have 20% cloaking and cost 20% less.
1129: Only half of your research resources go to the chosen field, but 15% of that amount goes to each of the other fields (125% in total).
1131: Scrapping a fleet at a station recovers 90% of its minerals and up to 70% of its resources, available the following year. At a planet without a station, half as much.
1132: Alchemy costs 25 resources instead of 100 to produce 1 kt of each mineral.
1134: No ramscoops (engines that collect fuel along the way). You get the Interstice 10, capable of safe Warp 10 much earlier.
1136: Engines 50% cheaper but unreliable: above Warp 6, a 10% chance per year that they refuse to start. +1 Propulsion level at the start.
1138: Only the Mini-miner is available for remote mining (cancels Advanced Remote Mining). Maximum population per planet +10%.
1140: No penetrating scanners, but the range of conventional scanners is doubled.
1142: You start with 30% fewer colonists (17,500 instead of 25,000).
1144: A new technology costs twice as much to build until you exceed all its prerequisites by one level. Miniaturization of 5% per level up to 80% (instead of 4% and 75%).
1146: Shields 40% stronger, regenerating 10% per round as long as they hold. Armor components are worth only 50% of their value.

1206: Research times are estimates, not exact: a breakthrough may come early or keep you waiting.
1208: Each game secretly shifts the level required for each technology (±2).
1210: Nebulae (scanners halved, Warp 6 maximum), drifting ion storms (shields halved) and dense clusters (rich, Warp 5 maximum).
1212: Output drops far from the capital and regional capitals; a conquered world takes a generation to reach full production; losing the capital throws the empire into disarray.
1214: Migration and mining policies: automatic convoys, real and interceptable, move colonists and minerals.
1216: Screen, line, artillery; threat-based targeting (no more cheap decoys soaking up fire); retreat thresholds.
1218: At certain levels, each empire chooses between two mutually exclusive, permanent doctrines.
1220: Long-term constructions that appear as research draws near them; one of them wins the game, and the whole galaxy follows its progress.
1222: Two hidden objectives per empire, revealed at the end; each one achieved earns score points.
1224: Without a penetrating scanner, the mass and number of detected fleets are estimates (±30%); holographic decoys inflate fleets.
1226: Anomalies to study with a scanner-equipped ship, archaeological sites to excavate chapter by chapter, relics, and the scattered map of the Ancients.
1227: Motionless, formidable fleets guard rich worlds far from the capitals. Defeating them yields research, minerals and sometimes a relic.
1229: Each empire chooses an origin (doomed world, relic world, lost colony...) that changes its start.
1230: Around 2415, pirate bands settle in lairs far from the capitals. Every few years, a raid plunders a rich, poorly defended colony. They can be paid to target a rival (an anonymous bounty); destroying a lair yields research and its loot.
1232: Around 2490-2520, depending on the size of the galaxy, a Breach opens far from the empires (announced ten years in advance). Its guardian, the Nexus, is stronger than any fleet in the galaxy, and waves of Reapers pour out of it to ravage the worlds of the most powerful. At the Breach, empires do not fight one another; whoever brings down the Nexus wins the game.
1234: War, peace or alliance between each pair of empires, trade and research agreements, tributes and gifts. Computer players hold an opinion of each empire, with its reasons, and respond to proposals according to rules shown in advance. You can only fight, invade and bomb empires you are at war with.
1236: What you know about other empires is built up over time: their worlds under your penetrating scanners or your ships in orbit, their identified ships, agreements and alliances, (reciprocal) embassies, spy networks, battles and conquests. The intelligence level (0 to 100) first reveals estimates, then the exact figures of their score, technology and fleet, and finally their research and secret objectives. Computer players judge your strength by what they know about you.
1238: Whoever holds the field after a battle studies the enemy wrecks: if they carried unknown components, its scientists progress toward them (a third of the next level in the field of the most advanced one), with better odds the more wrecks there are.
1240: Each colony radiates around it, ever farther with its population, its age and its cultural buildings. You cannot colonize within another empire's territory, and a world dominated by a foreign culture ends up joining it after a few decades.
